Monica / Jason — draft content below (Kimberly). I've kept the language short so it can be dropped into the CAIQ control response.

--- caiq-kv-affirmation.md (excerpt) ---
Redwood Inference assertion: Tenant KV caches used during model inference are logically segregated per-tenant and bound to runtime shards; cache entries do not cross tenant boundaries. In hosted deployments, KV cache instances are namespaced and access-controlled at the runtime layer. In private/VPC deployments, KV caching is constrained to customer-assigned nodes, with access gated by network policy and identity controls. Runtime-level telemetry records cache hits/misses and lifecycle events and these telemetry artifacts are available for audit with a retention policy of 90 days by default for hosted deployments; customers on Dedicated/Private can opt for custom retention through the Console.

Retention & access notes:
- Logs retained in encrypted object store (AES-256) for 90 days by default (hosted).
- Access to telemetry is restricted via RBAC; audit logs capture read access to artifacts.
- For private deployments, retention and storage location are controlled by the customer-managed environment.

--- end excerpt ---

I produced a sanitized log snippet (kv-cache-log-snippet-20270322.log) showing a single request lifecycle with masked identifiers. It's attached here as a text file; the .tar.gz contains a small packaged sample we use in CAIQ walk-throughs.

Redaction notes: Marissa used the standard redaction script to replace GUIDs, IPs, and model names with stable tokens (e.g., <TENANT_ID_***>, <NODE_ID>). See the attached redwood-scope-matrix for where this claim maps to CSA control IDs.

Let me know if Sterling needs a slightly different wording or if you'd like this certified by a security owner via DocuSign.

—Kimberly Park
